issue_context.title: [Feature]: Add ability to "Copy as Playwright Code" from traceviewer
issue_context.body:
### 🚀 Feature Request

As the team has recently added the functionality to copy http requests as cURL and as fetch, it would be great to have the option to copy the the http request to playwright code using the "request". This would allow someone to quickly post the playwright code into a playwright test or into a separate file to help build out a test data factory quickly. The big timesaver here is getting the headers and body created from the request.

### Example

After recording a playwright test, viewing an html report traceviewer, or after a playwright run while in ui mode, I could visit the network traffic tab, and right click a specific request and select copy as Playwright Code. 

### Motivation

This would help me build out helper functions to enable the creation test data.

review_comments: For JS, I wonder if JSON.stringify would do a similar job.
It would certainly output correct JS and be much less brittle, but it would contain lots of pesky double quotes that don't match the code style we have in the rest of the product.
This does not escape control characters like \n, \r, \t. `JSON.stringify(v)` would do a better job.

The problem with `JSON.stringify` is that it outputs double-quotes, and I want the outputted code to conform to the style we have in the rest of the product, which uses single quotes.

> This does not escape control characters like \n, \r, \t.

Good catch! I'll address that.
I've made it detect control characters and output them unescaped into source - I think the resulting code is easier to reason about than having a long string of escaped control characters.
i've added a fallback here to make types easier to reason about. this is only unavailable before the model is loaded, so falling back to `javascript` in a loading state is alright I feel.
